QUESTION:
What are the most common adverse reactions to Gabapentin?

RESPONSE:
The label excerpt I was given only covers the Indications and Usage and Dosage and Administration sections — it does not include the Adverse Reactions section, so I can't quote specific adverse reaction rates or lists from it.

For reference (from general gabapentin prescribing information, not from this excerpt), the most commonly reported adverse reactions include dizziness, somnolence (drowsiness), peripheral edema, ataxia/unsteadiness, fatigue, and, in pediatric patients, viral infection, fever, nausea/vomiting, and behavioral changes such as hostility or emotional lability. Gabapentin, like other antiepileptic drugs, also carries warnings about suicidal thoughts and behavior, and about respiratory depression when combined with opioids or other CNS depressants.

Please consult Section 6 (Adverse Reactions) and Section 5 (Warnings and Precautions) of the complete product labeling, or speak with your pharmacist or prescriber, for the authoritative and complete list.
